A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

people believe they are the subjects of others' attention more than they are the objects of others' attention and this is a widespread illusion that persists even when people's own behavior suggests that they are being observed as much as they observe others.
people are not as good at detecting when they are being observed as they think they are.
